questions: Does line_loss_events fall to 0 with the 8 mm footprint, or does one loss per run remain?
Does max_error drop below about 0.06 m, or does it stay at the off-track floor? If it stays there, geometry is exhausted.
Does the smaller footprint make the signal noisier (higher steering_oscillation above about 0.2), or does it stay in the 0.07 to 0.16 band?
Does progress change from the 0.10 to 0.18 band, or does the 8 mm footprint lose tape too early at the outer sensors?

intent: Test the 8 mm sensor footprint alone, keeping the iteration 7 geometry (y = 0.06 m, x = -0.04 to +0.04, track 0.10 m, wheel_radius 0.030 m, mass 0.4 kg, body 0.18 x 0.12 m). This is the only geometry change, so any change in line_loss_events or max_error is attributable to footprint. Expected result: line_loss_events falls toward 0 and max_error drops below about 0.06 m. If neither happens, geometry has nothing further to offer and the next work should be on the controller.
learning: Iterations 0 to 7 show that pitch, footprint at 12 to 16 mm, track, gain, mass, wheel_radius and lead (y = 0.04 to 0.06 m) have each left max_error at the 0.06 m floor and one line loss per run. The 8 mm footprint is the last untested geometry lever. If it does not clear the line loss, the geometry search is effectively exhausted and the remaining gain must come from the controller.
rationale: Evidence from iterations 0 to 7 (480 trials, all off_track) is consistent. max_error stays at the 0.060 to 0.068 m off-track floor on every track, and line_loss_events is 1 per run from iteration 3 onward. Pitch (10 to 20 mm), footprint (12 to 16 mm), track (0.12 to 0.10 m), gain (kp 1.4), mass (0.8 to 0.4 kg) and wheel_radius (0.035 m, which lowered progress and score in iteration 6) have each left max_error unchanged. Iteration 7 moved the sensor bar to y = 0.06 m, and the result was 53.4013, with max_error still at the floor (oval 0.0614, s-bend 0.0634, slalom 0.0673) and one line loss per run. Lead alone is therefore not enough. Following the Integrator's rule for this case, I keep y = 0.06 m, x = -0.04 to +0.04, track 0.10 m, wheel_radius 0.030 m and mass 0.4 kg, and change only sensor_size from 0.016 to 0.008 m, the one footprint size not yet tested. The 8 mm footprint gives sharper edge transitions and a smaller per-sensor coverage. This may reduce the outer-sensor dropout that causes the line loss, but it could also make the signal drop out sooner, so the result is uncertain. I expect line_loss_events to fall toward 0 and max_error to move below about 0.06 m, but I am not confident. If the line loss persists at 1 per run, the Geometry Builder's remaining geometry levers are exhausted and the controller, which is outside this role, is the likely limit.
